output.brief:
The complaints most likely come from contaminated brake fluid, not driver technique or the new pads. Northfield Motor Services changed fluid on 13 Eastgate vans while the in-house bay was closed. Eleven of those vans account for all 27 complaints. The other two Northfield vans got fluid from a freshly opened drum. Northfield used an old bulk drum with a replaced cap, and that drum had taken on water. Two vans tested on 24 Sep had fluid boiling at 152°C and 149°C. Sealed stock boils at 255°C. Water-laden fluid can vaporise in hot brakes on long descents and make the pedal go soft. The same 19 drivers had no brake reports in other vans, including 141 days on Upper Wend. That rules out technique and the hills as the main cause. Calder Road vans, which had the same pads, produced no complaints. Northfield warned Larkspur on 25 Sep, and nobody replied.

What to do this week: pull all 13 Northfield vans, including the two that look fine, and test and renew their fluid from sealed stock. Also check any other Northfield work from before 10 Sep. Do not discipline the drivers, because they reported a real fault. Hold off on changing pad supplier until there is evidence that the pads are a problem. I'm fairly confident in this, though I haven't tested the fluid in every van.
